title: Heterogeneous-attention onboarding: compile matrix, version pinning, and profile publication
creator: Marco Chen
description: Problem: We need a deterministic, testable workflow to onboard models that use mixed attention paradigms (MHA, GQA, MoE). Currently compilation heuristics and kernel selection are brittle across variant sizes and sharding strategies, causing regressions in latency or correctness after automatic kernel updates. This ticket defines the compile matrix, pinning policy for model versions, and a profile publishing pipeline so product teams can safely consume performance profiles and fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A reproducible compile matrix generator that enumerates model dimensions (sequence lengths, head/work grouping, expert-shard counts) and target architectures (A100, H100, L4) for MHA/GQA/MoE variants.
2) A pinning API/metadata format is implemented so a model version can declare an explicit kernel profile SHA and fallback list in the model catalog.
3) CI jobs validate each compiled bundle against correctness tests and representative latency P95 targets.
4) Published performance profiles (JSON) land in the model catalog UI and the runtime can consume them by model-version.
5) Rollout and rollback playbook documented and automated gating exists to prevent unsafe profile promotion.
6) Telemetry emits kernel_version, profile_id, observed_p95, and kv_cache_hit_ratio for every request to support regressions detection.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1: Matrix generator and test harness
- Implement a YAML-driven matrix generator that emits compile permutations for MHA/GQA/MoE (shard counts, expert counts, head groupings, dtype/quantization flags, seq_len buckets).
- Add unit tests and a small dataset of synthetic inputs to exercise correctness (logits/softmax invariants).
Phase 2: CI compile and verification
- Extend CI to start containerized compile jobs per matrix entry and run deterministic inference checks + latency microbenchmarks.
Phase 3: Pin format & catalog publishing
- Define a pin schema (profile_id, kernel_sha, supported_shapes, validated_commit, confidence_score) and wire it into model-onboarder.
- Add a lightweight API to publish a profile to the model catalog and attach to a model-version.
Phase 4: Runtime consumption & fallbacks
- Runtime reads pinned profile for model-version and enforces kernel selection; if incompatible, falls back to reference kernel and emits a fault metric.
Phase 5: Rollout automation & alerting
- Create a promotion pipeline (canary -> regional rollouts) that monitors p95, error-rate, and KV cache effectiveness before full promotion.
rollout_plan:
- Start with a single non-critical internal model (mosaic-m) as canary.
- Canary window (48h) with heavy synthetic and sampled production traffic.
- Automatic revert if p95 regresses >10% or request error-rate increases by 0.5%.
- After stability, expand to 3 additional models across different size classes.
- Full promotion requires signoff by runtime lead and release engineering.
telemetry_and_dashboards:
- New dashboard: 'Profile Onboarding' shows per-profile p95, p50, error rate, kernel_sha, and kv_cache_hit_ratio.
- Alerting rules: p95-up-by-10pct, error-rate-up-by-0.5pct, unexpected-fallback-rate>1%.
- Logs: structured events for profile_published, profile_promoted, profile_reverted with links to CI artifacts and compile logs.
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: Compiled kernels produce subtle numerical differences leading to quality regressions. Mitigation: include unit-level probabilistic checks (token distribution stats) and human review for models with eval suites.
- Risk: Matrix explosion causing long CI times. Mitigation: prune shapes via telemetry-driven footprint (only compile top N shapes covering 95% of traffic) and apply incremental compiles.
- Risk: Incorrect pin metadata causes runtime mismatch. Mitigation: strong validation in the publish API and staging catalog visible to ops before promotion.
